leitz-lexicon-7-drilling.notes: the printed tool tables: speed range, diameter range, material list, machine list, chip-clearing rules and the feed correction factor tables

leitz-lexicon-7-drilling-chart-read.document: vector-path read of the feed-speed diagrams printed beside the tool tables in Leitz Lexicon Edition 7 chapter 6
leitz-lexicon-7-drilling-chart-read.method: polygon vertex coordinates taken from the PDF vector art, sliced by crossing every edge of the outline at the sampled speed rather than by sampling nearby vertices. A diagram is accepted only when its band overlaps the tool's published speed range and covers at least the fraction named in rules.drilling.band_coverage_min, its own printed worked operating point converts (fn = vf * 1000 / n) and lands inside the band read off it, the axis calibration residual is under 2% of the range, and a baseline material and factor table are printed under it. Seventeen of the eighteen in-scope diagrams pass; the eighteenth, the boring pins, prints no factor table. All seventeen print a worked operating point and all seventeen land inside their own band.
leitz-lexicon-7-drilling-chart-read.notes: the diagrams plot feed speed against spindle speed for one baseline material. The band is an operating range, not a diameter spread: the single-diameter 35 mm turnblade tool carries the same 2:1 ratio as the 15-40 mm hinge drill at the same speed.

material_factor_map.note: which calculator material reads as which printed factor row. The printed factor vocabulary is its own namespace and deliberately does not extend the routing material list, because Leitz names rows the calculator has no pick for (veneered chipboard, glulam). Candidates are ordered: the first one an entry's own factor table publishes wins. When an entry publishes none of them, the most conservative published factor serves with a note (Scott, 2026-09-02, decision 9), because refusing a pick the tool's own material list covers would be a refusal the source does not make. Two orderings are deliberate. The plain MDF pick reads only the plain MDF row: the solid-carbide hinge drills publish a 'MDF plastic coated' row at 1.0 and no plain row, and letting plain MDF take it served a coated-panel feed for an uncoated board, unmarked, at more than twice the factor every other section prints for MDF. That coated row belongs to the melamine pick instead, which is what a plastic-coated panel is, so it sits second behind coated chipboard there. A pick that falls through to the conservative fallback can end up under the chip floor, which rubs and burns rather than cutting. The calculator raises such a feed to the thinnest chip that still cuts, no further than the tool's own unfactored value at that profile and speed, and says on the page that it did (Scott, 2026-09-02). Where even that ceiling sits under the floor the feed cannot be rescued and a warning stands instead.

profiles.note: gentle = the low edge of the published feed band at the served speed, standard = its midpoint, aggressive = its high edge. The midpoint is Scott's call (2026-09-02, decision 8), taken so that the three words mean the same thing in drilling as in routing. The cost is recorded, and it is not a constant: across the twelve tools the vendor's own marked operating point sits anywhere from 22% to 93% up its band, so Standard runs from 20% under that point to 26% over it, below on nine tools and above on three. An earlier version of this note generalised 'about 11% under' from the hinge drill alone, which was the same mistake the band-ratio figure had already made. Every tool's marked point renders as a marker on the feed chart, at the speed it was printed for, so the user can see where the source itself sits. Finishing is not offered, because a hole has no finish pass and no source publishes a finishing drill feed.

entries.label: Dowel drill
entries.teeth_source: GL 55.5 mm, with heel, Z 2 / V 2
entries.materials_printed: Softwood and hardwood, chipboard and fibre materials (MDF, HDF etc.), uncoated, plastic coated, veneered etc., laminated veneer lumber (plywood, multiplex plywood etc.).
entries.machines_printed: Point-to-point drilling machines, through feed drilling machines, CNC machining centres, hinge boring machines, multi spindle units.
entries.notes: Section 6.1.1, blind holes for dowels in furniture construction. Spur geometry with shear cut. The four shank variants of this tool (8 mm, 10 mm, threaded, and the version without a heel) print one shared feed diagram, one speed range and one factor table, so they are one entry. The diameter range is the union of their own tables. Leitz does not state the cutting material for this tool in text; the grade recorded here follows the section structure, where 6.1.2 and 6.1.3 are published as the tipped and solid upgrades of it.

entries.label: Through-hole drill, solid carbide
entries.materials_printed: Softwood and hardwood, chipboard and fibre materials (MDF, HDF etc.), uncoated, plastic coated, veneered etc., laminated veneer lumber (plywood, multiplex plywood etc.).
entries.machines_printed: Point-to-point drilling machines, through feed drilling machines, CNC machining centres, hinge boring machines, multi spindle units.
entries.notes: Section 6.2.3. V-point tip with two bevels, solid tungsten carbide. The tool is rated to 12,000 rpm but its diagram draws the band only to about 9,000, so the band covers part of the speed range and the feed holds at that edge above it. Its diagram is the same artwork Leitz prints for 6.2.2, which is why the two bands match.

entries.machines_printed: Point-to-point drilling machines, through feed drilling machines, CNC machining centres, hinge boring machines, multi spindle units.

Diamond tipped, and rated by Leitz for abrasive board: gypsum-bonded, cement-bonded and flame-resistant particle and fibre materials, solid resin glulam and fibre-reinforced plastics. Its printed workpiece list carries no solid timber, so solid timber is outside its scope. One cutting edge, not two.

entries.label: Hinge drill, solid carbide, three edge
entries.materials_printed: Softwood and hardwood, chipboard and fibre materials (MDF, HDF etc.), uncoated, plastic coated, veneered etc., laminated veneer lumber (plywood, multiplex plywood etc.).
entries.machines_printed: Point-to-point drilling machines, through feed drilling machines, CNC machining centres, hinge boring machines, multi spindle units.
entries.notes: Section 6.3.2, part WB 320 0 13. Three cutting edges and three spurs where the other solid-carbide hinge drill has two, which is Leitz's own stated reason for its higher feed band: the page says it is designed for higher feed speed in comparison to boring bits with Z 2 / V 2. It shares its factor table with WB 310 0 13 but prints its own diagram and its own worked example, so it is a separate entry.

It is the evidence that the band width is an operating range and not a diameter spread: a single-diameter tool carries the same band as the 15-40 mm hinge drill at the same speed.

entries.label: Levin drill, high speed steel
entries.machines_printed: Column drilling machines, drilling machines, multi spindle units, special purpose drilling machines, portable drills.
entries.notes: Section 6.4.2, deep holes in solid timber. A spiral flute with a large chip gullet, which is why it reaches four times its diameter with no clearing stroke at all.
